chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Abi Najran from Sabbah al-Hazza' from a man from Abu Hamza said:

Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said: "O Thumamah, indeed when the prayer is established, Satan comes to the companion of the Imam and says: 'Did he remember his Lord?' If he says yes, he departs, and if he says no, he mounts upon his shoulders and remains the leader of the people until they turn away."
I said, 'May I be your ransom, do they not recite the Quran?' He said, 'Yes, but it is not where you think, O Thumamah; rather it is the vocalizing of "Bismillah ir-Rahman ir-Rahim."'
19 - Sahl ibn Ziyad from Muhammad ibn 'Abdus from Muhammad ibn Zadawayh from Ibn Rashid said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), 'May I be your ransom, you wrote to Muhammad ibn al-Faraj informing him that the best that is recited in the obligatory prayers is "Inna anzalnahu" and "Qul huwa Allahu ahad", and indeed my chest feels constrained by reciting them in the dawn prayer.'
He said (peace be upon him), "Let not your chest be constrained by them, for the excellence is, by God, in them."

key_terms.بِسْمِ اَللّهِ اَلرَّحْمَنِ اَلرَّحِيمِ: The Basmala (In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful)
key_terms.قَرِينِ اَلْإِمَامِ: The companion of the Imam (referring to Satan or a spiritual companion)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of vocalizing the Basmala during prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: The first narration highlights the spiritual vulnerability of the Imam during the opening of prayer, where Satan attempts to disrupt focus by questioning the vocalization of the Basmala, a key element in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the prayer's validity. The second narration addresses the concern of brevity in reciting Surah Al-Ikhlas and Al-Duha during Fajr, with Imam al-Sadiq reassuring that their profound theological weight compensates for their short length, affirming the principle that quality of devotion outweighs quantity of recitation.
